text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The West Indian cricket team has dismissed the Sydney cricket ground's spin and Shane Warne as serious threats to their cricket game. The West Indies have a poor track record at Sydney having never won a game there for over 35 years. Page 22.

A readers' poll in the latest Wisden Cricket Monthly has selected five Australians to play in the World cricket team. The five were Mark Taylor as captain, Mark and Steve Waugh, Ian Healy and Shane Warne. Only one Australian, Michael Slater, made the World Second XI. Page 22.

Olympic gold medallist Susie O'Neill has again been selected by her sports peers as a top athlete, winning the 1996 Queensland Sportsperson of the year. O'Neill was chosen over sporting greats such as golfer Karrie Webb, motorcycle champion Michael Doohan and triathlete Jackie Gallagher. Page 22.

Shane Heal, who now plays in the National Basketball Association in the United States, yesterday lit up a career-high of 15 points against the Seattle Supersonics. However, his game for the Minnesota Timberwolves was not good enough, with his team going own 106-98. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

West Indian cricket coach Malcolm Marshall yesterday spoke out against questions that his batsmen could not play spin, saying that they had beaten the Indian team in India and the Pakistan team in Pakistan and that his batsman could play just as well on Sydney's grassless pitch against Australia. Page 46.

Australia's rugby union coach Greg Smith has put on hold his decision to select the final XV to play against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park on Sunday for 24-hours, putting in doubt David Campese's selection for the game. Smith instead named a 21-man squad, which did not include Daniel Manu and included David Giffin to replace an injured John Eales. Page 46.

Phil Coles, an International Olympic Committee delegate, has dismissed a suggestion by Prince Alexandre de Merode, the head of the medical commission, that bans for athletes who fail drug tests be shortened. Coles sayd he thought the prince was just statng his own views and few would agree with them. Page 46.

The Sydney Swans have gained an excellent start to next year with the AFL shaping next year's season to allow more of the popular night games and eight of the Swan's 11 at home games to be played against good crowd pulling teams. Page 45.
THE AGE

Lucas Parsons of New South Wales has finally found his golfing form at Royal Melbourne yesterday in the A$700,000 Greg Norman Classic to hold the lead with a score of five under par, 67. Parsons has had a dreadful debut season so far this year, only making the cut in five of his 23 tournaments. Page C12.

Ross Oakley yesterday just about cancelled any hope of his joining the organising committee for the Sydney Olympic Games as a senior executive, saying he was "looking for a life after sport" and taking on such an appointment would be tantamount to "jumping out of the pot and into the fire". Page C10.

Stewards yesterday decided not to pursue Mornington trainer David Racovlis on a prohibited substance charge over his mare Eastern Princess. Eastern Princess was disqualified from her win in the Tesio Stakes at Moonee Valley on 26 October on a charge she won the race with the aid of an anabolic steroid. Page C10.

Mark Philippoussis put in a rare appearance yesterday at the relaunch of a tennis magazine, but the media that turned up in the hope of scooping a story on his sacking of three coaches this year was lost when he left after a brief announcement and the siging of a few posters for charity. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

The AFL yesterday announced the creation of five Monday night games for the 1997 season, boosting the number on last year's. The number of night games in total for the season will be 53, making night games 30 percent of all AFL games and further confirming the AFL's push to harness what was last year a successful match time. Page 112.

The Brisbane Football Club may be forced to pay A$500,000 in compensation for using the name the Brisbane Lions, with the Brisbane Lions soccer club beginning legal action to stop the AFL club from using their team's name. Page 110.

The Carlton Soccer Club will continue to look overseas for candidates for its coaching position but has confirmed in the meantime it will appoint an Australian coach. The move to include overseas Australians brings Ken Worden and Ron Smith into calculaions. Page 102.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
